title: Finite pushforward preserves and reflects finite presentation near a singleton fibre
statement: Let $p:T\to U$ be a finite morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] that is of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], let $t\in T$ and $u=p(t)$, and assume $p^{-1}(\{u\})=\{t\}$. For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal M$ on $T$ [pqf-def-coherent], $\mathcal M$ is of finite presentation on a neighbourhood of $t$ if and only if $p_*\mathcal M$ is of finite presentation on a neighbourhood of $u$ [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. Moreover, $\mathcal M_t$ is finitely presented over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ if and only if $(p_*\mathcal M)_u$ is finitely presented over $\mathcal O_{U,u}$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Here $p_*\mathcal M$ is the Zariski direct image: for an open $V\subseteq U$, $(p_*\mathcal M)(V)=\mathcal M(p^{-1}V)$ with $\mathcal O_U(V)$ acting through $p^\sharp(V):\mathcal O_U(V)\to\mathcal O_T(p^{-1}V)$; the stalks and their scalar actions are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk].

source.place: Tag 057T, proof paragraph beginning “Using Descent, Lemma 03C4 ...”; stalk paragraph using More on Morphisms Tag 0A1H.

proof.text: For any open neighbourhood $W$ of $t$, the set $C=T\setminus W$ is closed and $p(C)$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres](1). Since the entire fibre over $u$ is $\{t\}$, we have $u\notin p(C)$. Thus $V_0=U\setminus p(C)$ is an open neighbourhood of $u$ with $p^{-1}V_0\subseteq W$. Choose an affine open $u\in V\subseteq V_0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Consequently inverse images of affine neighbourhoods of $u$ are cofinal among all neighbourhoods of $t$.

Let $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ be any affine neighbourhood of $u$. Finiteness of $p$ means $p^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}S$ is affine and $R\to S$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Since $p$ is locally of finite presentation, [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] applied to these two affine opens makes $R\to S$ finitely presented as an algebra. Put $N=\Gamma(p^{-1}V,\mathcal M)$. The direct image is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change](1), since $p$ is affine and $\mathcal M$ is quasi-coherent. Its module of sections on $V$ is $N$ regarded as an $R$-module: [lem-weil-pbc-pushforward-spec-global-sections] identifies the scalar action with restriction of scalars along $R\to S$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](b) on $p^{-1}V$ and on $V$. It identifies finite presentation of $\mathcal M|_{p^{-1}V}$ with finite presentation of $N$ over $S$, and finite presentation of $(p_*\mathcal M)|_V$ with finite presentation of the same $N$ over $R$. All hypotheses hold by Step 2. The hypotheses that $S$ is finitely generated as an $R$-module and finitely presented as an $R$-algebra therefore allow [lem-trf-finite-extension-module-finite-presentation] to give
$$\mathcal M|_{p^{-1}V}\text{ is of finite presentation}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad(p_*\mathcal M)|_V\text{ is of finite presentation}.$$

proof.text: The map $\theta:(p_*\mathcal M)_u\to\mathcal M_t$ sends the germ at $u$ of a section $s\in\mathcal M(p^{-1}V)$ to its germ at $t$. This is bijective directly from [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] and Step 1: every germ at $t$ is represented on some $W\ni t$ and can be restricted to $p^{-1}V\subseteq W$, proving surjectivity. If two such sections have equal germs at $t$, they agree on a neighbourhood $W\subseteq p^{-1}(V_1\cap V_2)$ of $t$; Step 1 gives a neighbourhood $V_3\subseteq V_1\cap V_2$ of $u$ with $p^{-1}V_3\subseteq W$, so their germs at $u$ agree, proving injectivity. If $a\in\mathcal O_U(V)$ and $s\in\mathcal M(p^{-1}V)$, then $\theta((a\cdot s)_u)=(p^\sharp(a)s)_t=p_t^\sharp(a_u)\,\theta(s_u)$. Hence $\theta$ is an $\mathcal O_{U,u}$-linear isomorphism when $\mathcal M_t$ has its scalar action restricted through $p_t^\sharp$.

source.place: Tag 05B8(4), final proof sentence: alternative proof from (1) and the definition of stalks, written out.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-finite-singleton-fibre-stalk-ring], the canonical map $p_t^\sharp:\mathcal O_{U,u}\to\mathcal O_{T,t}$ is finite and finitely presented: $p$ is finite and finitely presented and its fibre over $u$ is exactly $\{t\}$, as required. Apply [lem-trf-finite-extension-module-finite-presentation] to this ring map and the $\mathcal O_{T,t}$-module $\mathcal M_t$. Its hypotheses hold because $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ is finitely generated as an $\mathcal O_{U,u}$-module and finitely presented as an $\mathcal O_{U,u}$-algebra, and it gives finite presentation over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ if and only if finite presentation over $\mathcal O_{U,u}$. The $\mathcal O_{U,u}$-linear identification in Step 5 identifies the latter module with $(p_*\mathcal M)_u$, proving the asserted stalkwise equivalence.
